paper_code_mismatch: The code parse is of the present-day (2025/2026-era) isaac-sim/IsaacLab repository, ORBIT's renamed successor, not a 2023 snapshot; any dexterous-suite detail found there (e.g. a KUKA+Allegro lift/grasp/reorient task suite) postdates this paper and must not be attributed to it.
note_gaps: No numeric default timestep/substeps is stated (simulation frequency and decimation are treated only as comparison-fairness knobs); no solver-family name or iteration counts (LCP/PGS/TGS/Newton/CG) are given; no numeric contact-point count per geometry pair; Fig. 12/13 throughput-comparison curve values and Table II imitation-learning success-rate/trajectory-length cells did not survive parsing from the source; deformable-body sim-to-real fidelity was validated on only one controlled setup (a clamped silicone beam), not the general task suite; the second of the paper's two named 'robotic hands' (Sec. IV-a) is never identified by name anywhere in the text.
contact_model: PhysX SDK 5 signed-distance-field (SDF) collision checking for rigid bodies (handles non-convex geometry such as screw threads); FEM-based solver using a constraint-based stable neo-hookean material formulation for deformable bodies; PBD (position-based dynamics) solver for cloth
solver: PhysX SDK 5's internal rigid-body and FEM solvers, used as-is; no LCP/PGS/TGS, Newton, or CG iteration counts given
throughput: 125,000 FPS physics-only ceiling (no env count stated); ~10x rigid-body throughput vs. CPU-vectorized frameworks (robosuite, ManiSkill2, IsaacGymEnvs) swept 256-4096 envs; ~3x deformable/cloth throughput vs. DEDO; 270 FPS aggregate for 10 cameras at 640x480; hardware: 16-core AMD Ryzen 5950X, 64GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3090 (Sec. V-E-b, VII)
